item.title: Component Constructor
item.description: The OCM Component Constructor defines the input format for building component versions. It describes how resources and sources are provided – either via access specifications (referencing existing artifacts) or via input specifications (providing content directly).

item.title: Component Descriptor
item.description: The OCM Component Descriptor is the central data structure of the Open Component Model. It describes a component version with its resources, sources, references, labels, and signatures.

item.title: Input and Access Types
item.description:
Overview

Resources in a component version are added using either an input type or an access type.

  • Input type — embeds content by value. The content is stored alongside the component descriptor in the target repository.
  • Access type — stores an access specification pointing to the content. In the constructor, this typically references an external location (e.g. an OCI registry) rather than embedding the content.

A resource must have exactly one of input or access. See the Component Constructor reference for the full YAML schema.

item.title: Resource Repositories
item.description: This page is the technical reference for built-in resource repositories. For an introduction to what resource repositories are and why they exist, see Concept: Resource Repositories.

item.title: OCI Resource Digests
item.description: An OCM resource digest records a hash algorithm, a normalisation algorithm, and a value. All three fields affect the signed component descriptor and component reference digests. Changing the normalisation name changes the descriptor’s identity, even if the hash value stays the same. See Signing and Verification for how resource digests participate in signatures.
